nearest_prs.read: Body read: put a lid into a light case's pocket, press its front edge until two spring latches click while the other arm steadies the tipping case.
nearest_prs.comparison: Shared: press a hinged/fitted lid's front until a spring catch clicks. Theirs is an assembly job on a labelled case whose instruction names the lid closing. Ours is an unnamed hazard: the instruction is only 'Prepare the kettle for use'; the robot must notice a lid resting proud on a real 1.7 L kettle's catch, press it with a controlled force without tipping a 2 kg full kettle off its fixed power base, and release fully.

nearest_prs.read: Body read: push a popped jester back into a jack-in-the-box and shut the lid so its catch holds.
nearest_prs.comparison: Toy reset: compressing a spring figure is the difficulty; no hazard, no heavy free-standing container on a base.

nearest_prs.read: Body read: seat both AirPods in their wells and push the magnetic lid shut.
nearest_prs.comparison: Small-part insertion is the difficulty; the lid is magnetic, no catch to press past, no tipping/scald hazard.

nearest_prs.read: Body and review read: fill a 0.39-scale kettle between MIN and MAX and shut the lid; rejected for miniaturization and capacity inconsistencies.
nearest_prs.comparison: Pouring/fill-level task at reduced scale. Ours is real scale (25 cm, 1.7 L, 2.0 kg with 1 L) and the skill is the lid latch recovery, not filling; the reviewer's scale objection does not apply.

physical_skill: Notice that the kettle's hinged lid rests on its spring catch 5 degrees open, press its front edge down with about 12 N until it clicks within 0.4 degrees of shut, without tipping the free-standing 2 kg kettle more than 15 degrees or knocking it off its 17.6 cm power base, then withdraw every fingertip at least 3 cm.
valid_shortcuts: Red team on this task.py: do nothing 0; hold on the lid after clicking 0.5; careless shove of the body then press 0 (tilt 85 degrees). Pressing the release button after latching returns the lid to its catch, scoring 0. Lifting the kettle off its base or opening and re-closing the lid are legitimate and still require a latched, seated, untouched final state for 3 s. Valid solution: press the lid's front down (demo 1.0 twice). Dream-1 this session: 0 (both arms moved forward and hovered beside the kettle but never pressed the lid).
distinct_from_nearest: No live task involves an electric kettle or its lid latch; the only kettle task (1406) was a miniaturized fill task, closed. The nearest skill match is the accepted snap-fit case lid (32), but that task names the closing and is an assembly job; ours is a goal-only, unnamed scald hazard on a real-scale full kettle with a tip/displacement constraint. Residual risk: a reviewer may see it as one more 'press a lid until it clicks' task or judge the press too easy.
